summary: The facelifted 2026 Solterra addresses the original car's biggest weaknesses, gaining a larger 74.7kWh battery, more power (252kW combined) and up to 566km of WLTP range, backed by two rounds of price cuts in six months that make it far more competitive. Australian reviewers rate the driving experience highly - composed, quick and comfortable - and praise the upgraded, more premium-feeling cabin, though they still mark it down for tight practicality, some cabin ergonomic quirks and a ride that could use further tuning. Several reviewers suggest the entry AWD variant is the sweet spot of the range, rather than the higher-priced Touring.
pros: Major step up over the outgoing model: bigger battery, +92kW more power and notably longer range
Composed, quick and engaging to drive - CarsGuide rated the driving experience 9/10
Upgraded, more premium-feeling interior with a redesigned console and larger touchscreen
Two price cuts within six months have made it meaningfully more competitive against rivals like the Tesla Model Y and BYD Sealion 7
Standard AWD on both variants with a useful 1,500kg tow rating, unusual for a mid-size EV SUV at this price
cons: Practicality trails rivals - CarsGuide scored it just 5/10 on practicality, citing tight boot space and no passenger-side glovebox
Ride quality still needs further tuning - reviewers describe it as firm with more bounciness than ideal
Cabin ergonomic quirks, including an instrument display that can be partly obstructed and an intrusive driver-monitoring system
Repeated price cuts so soon after launch raise doubts about resale value and initial pricing
Touring grade seen as poor value next to the base AWD, which reviewers say is the better buy in the range
